MAJOR: CI detachment neuters the gate: `--head` derives the branch via `rev-parse --abbrev-ref HEAD`; on a PR/merge-ref checkout that yields `HEAD`, so `branch_id` is empty → the "blocking" ci-cd-gates entry always warns-and-passes in CI, giving false assurance at exactly the merge boundary the ticket targets.

`"branch-item": "structure"` was added to `_GROUP_OF`, but the diff never shows a `structure` group declared in precheck's gate-group registry; if absent this raises KeyError and breaks the entire precheck fast tier.

`_git` discards stderr and ignores return codes; any git failure (shallow clone, no commits, detached worktree) yields empty branch/message → silently warn-and-pass. The guard should fail closed or explicitly distinguish "no branch" from "git error".

Bypass by construction: the merge/revert skip is a first-line `startswith("Merge "/"Revert ")` sniff with no parent-count check, so any commit prefixed `Merge ` evades the guard; use `git rev-list --parents -n 1 HEAD` (or `--no-merges` semantics) instead of message heuristics.

No documentation update to docs/ENGINEERING_OPERATING_STANDARD.md or docs/ARCHITECTURE-DECISIONS.md for a new enforced, blocking dev-workflow gate — the operating contract and the rationale (EDP-16 contamination) live only in a docstring.
MINOR: `--head` validates only the single last commit; a branch with N contaminated earlier commits passes as long as HEAD is clean — the "before merge" re-check is weaker than its name implies.
Normalization treats `BI-1308` and `BI-PF-1308` as distinct ids; a message using the short form fails against a `BI-PF-*` branch (and vice versa), producing false blocks.
The "no branch id" path prints `OK (...)` rather than `WARN`, muddying observability for the develop/release warn-only requirement; exit code is right, semantics are unlabeled.
Message ids are scanned across the whole body, so a stale `Refs: BI-PF-XXXX` footer lets a mismatched commit through; restricting to subject + explicit trailer would tighten integrity.

Tests cover only `check()`; no coverage of `--message-file`/`--head` paths, revert skip (criteria mention revert), or the installed hook, and the `sys.path.insert` import hack diverges from any shared test harness convention.

New shipped-ish logic in Python is defensible as tooling, but the ticket's spirit ("guards that gate delivery") may drift into shipped domain logic; a Go port decision should be recorded, not implied.
NIT: `_COMMITMSG` invokes bare `python`; if sibling hooks use `python3` or a venv interpreter this hook silently no-ops or errors on machines where `python` is absent.
The commit-msg hook has no `--amend`/`--allow-empty` tolerance note and no exec bit/permissions handling visible; verify `_install` preserves mode 0755.
Hook hardcodes the `product-forge/` layout prefix and exits 0 if missing — fine, but a comment tying it to the monorepo root contract would prevent a silent future no-op.
SUMMARY: Solid, well-scoped guard with correct warn-vs-block semantics for id-less branches and a clean shared `check()` core reused by both hook and precheck.
Top risks: the gate is effectively inert in CI due to detached-HEAD branch detection, git failures fail open, and the merge/revert skip is spoofable via message prefix.
Secondary: possible undefined `structure` gate group crashing precheck fast, and the new enforced gate is undocumented in the operating standard.
Verdict: right idea and right layering; needs hardening (parent-count merge detection, fail-closed git handling, CI branch checkout, docs) before it can be trusted as a blocking integrity control.
